headlines.title: China’s factory-gate prices growth slows to 3.5% in July amid lower fuel prices
headlines.summary:
China’s factory-gate prices growth slowed in July, as lower domestic fuel prices eased cost pressures triggered by the US-Israel war on Iran, while high temperatures dragged manufacturing.
The producer price index (PPI) rose by 3.5 per cent year on year last month, compared with 4.1 per cent in June, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Sunday.

headlines.title: 高盛：全球AI投资今年将突破10000亿美元 美国投资接近6000亿美元
headlines.summary: 近日，高盛分析师发布报告称，预计到2026年底，全球人工智能投资将超过1万亿美元，其中美国人工智能投资预计接近6000亿美元。高盛研究部根据其对人工智能投资的偏好估计值，推算出到2028年人工智能投资占美国GDP的比例。据高盛估算，美国人工智能资本支出占GDP的比重将从2026年的1.8%上升到2027年的2.5%，并在2028年进一步上升到2.8%。而与此同时，全球人工智能投资占全球GDP的比重，将在2026年至2028年逐年上升，分别为0.9%、1.3%和1.4%。（财联社）

headlines.title_en: Goldman Sachs: Global AI investment to exceed $1 trillion this year, with US investment nearing $600 billion
headlines.summary_en: Recently, Goldman Sachs analysts released a report forecasting that global AI investment will exceed $1 trillion by the end of 2026, with U.S. AI investment expected to approach $600 billion. Based on its estimated preferences for AI investment, Goldman Sachs Research calculated the share of AI investment in U.S. GDP by 2028. According to Goldman Sachs estimates, U.S. AI capital expenditure as a share of GDP will rise from 1.8% in 2026 to 2.5% in 2027, and further to 2.8% in 2028. Meanwhile, global AI investment as a share of global GDP will rise year by year from 2026 to 2028, at 0.9%, 1.3%, and 1.4%, respectively. (Cailianshe)

headlines.title: 退市新规征求意见，全球芯片LOF跌停，白银LOF重挫
headlines.summary: 一早盘，多只前期高溢价LOF同步回调。其中，全球芯片LOF跌停，但溢价仍居高不下、维持在18%；国投白银LOF盘中一度大跌超8%，溢价率同样突破18%。行情异动或源于上周末的重磅监管新规。沪深交易所联合发布LOF退市新规征求意见稿，明确两类产品强制退市情形，精准直击场内LOF长期存在的高溢价投机炒作、迷你基金流动性枯竭、价格易被操纵等市场顽疾。沪上一位公募人士受访称，对于当前溢价率较高的QDII或商品期货LOF，退市预期或将直接打击投机情绪。（一财）

headlines.title_en: New delisting rules for public comment; global chip LOF hits limit down, silver LOF drops sharply
headlines.summary_en: In early trading, several LOFs with high premiums from earlier periods pulled back simultaneously. Among them, Global Chip LOF hit the limit down, but the premium remained high at 18%; SDIC Silver LOF fell over 8% intraday, with its premium also exceeding 18%. The unusual market moves may stem from heavy regulatory rules announced last weekend. The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges jointly issued a draft for comment on new delisting rules for LOFs, specifying two types of mandatory delisting situations, precisely targeting long-standing market ills such as speculative trading at high premiums, liquidity drying up in mini funds, and price manipulation in on-exchange LOFs. A public fund insider in Shanghai said in an interview that for QDII or commodity futures LOFs with high premiums, delisting expectations could directly dampen speculative sentiment. (Yicai)

headlines.title_en: Morning market wrap on August 10: ChiNext Index falls over 2% in half-day trading; pharmaceutical and consumer stocks buck trend to strengthen
headlines.summary_en: 1. Markets diverged clearly in the morning; the Shanghai Composite traded in positive territory, while the ChiNext Index fell over 2%. Pharma stocks continued their gains, with Baihua Pharma hitting a five-day limit-up streak, and multiple stocks such as Yatai Pharmacy, Hayao, and Haisco Pharmaceutical hitting limit-up. Consumer stocks like food strengthened against the trend, with Huangshi Group, Xiangpiaopiao, and Yiming Food hitting limit-up. The defense sector saw a surge, with Hunan Tianyan and Great Wall Military hitting limit-up. On the downside, computing-hardware stocks such as PCB and CPO fell, with Accelink Technologies nearing limit-down, and Changyingtong and Taijin New Energy falling over 10%. Advancers outnumbered decliners, with over 3,400 stocks rising across the Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Beijing markets, and turnover reaching RMB 1.75 trillion in the morning half-session. At midday close, the Shanghai Composite rose 0.2%, the Shenzhen Component fell 1.13%, and the ChiNext fell 2.18%. 2.
